generations.prompt: An old woman in a mustard cardigan sits on a timber porch in warm late-afternoon sun, speaking to a small cloth-covered device on the table beside her. She is amused and exacting, a teacher correcting a pupil she likes. She speaks a soft, unfamiliar, vowel-rich language of her own, not English, with the stress late in each word. She shakes her head once and says: "Voké ru." (voh-kéh roo). A short pause. Then, slowly and clearly, lifting one finger, she says the single word: "Noréla." (no-réh-la), with the weight on the middle syllable. She keeps her eyes on the device, never on the camera. Sound: her voice, wind in dry grass, insects. The camera is locked off and does not move. No music. No subtitles, captions or on-screen text of any kind.
